topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links by introducing periodic variations in the antenna pattern. This can lead to a reduction in directivity and an increase in side lobes, compromising beamforming gain and SINR. The optimal interleaved spacing depends on the specific antenna design and operating frequency. As a general principle, reducing the spacing can improve grating lobe suppression but may also increase the risk of inter-beam interference.
